Sputnik. Sputnik one was the world's first artificial satellite, launched by the Soviet Union on October fourth, nineteen fifty-seven. Its beeping radio signals circling the Earth shocked the Western world and ignited the Space Race, spurring the United States to found NASA and commit to space exploration as a Cold War imperative. Sputnik became a symbol of Soviet technological prowess and American vulnerability, reshaping geopolitical competition and science education globally.

Sputnik was launched on October fourth, nineteen fifty-seven, from Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan. It was a fifty-eight-centimeter polished steel sphere weighing eighty-four kilograms, equipped with four external radio antennas. It orbited Earth every ninety-six minutes at altitudes between two hundred twenty-eight and nine hundred forty-seven kilometers, transmitting a simple beep-beep radio signal on twenty point zero zero five megahertz.

The Western response was panic. Americans feared Soviet intercontinental ballistic missiles could reach any target on Earth. Sputnik was perceived as evidence that the Soviets were technologically ahead, a stark reversal of assumed American dominance. It generated an admissions panic—concern that American science education was failing and needed urgent reform. Soviet First Secretary Nikita Khrushchev made triumphant claims of Communist superiority.

Sputnik prompted President Eisenhower to approve the creation of NASA in October nineteen fifty-eight with a mandate to restore American leadership in space. It triggered the American education system to emphasize science, technology, engineering, and mathematics curricula, and Congress passed the National Defense Education Act in nineteen fifty-eight. The launch of the Space Race followed: the United States launched Explorer one in January nineteen fifty-eight and then committed to the Moon-landing goal a few years later under Kennedy. Sputnik one decayed and re-entered Earth's atmosphere on January fourth, nineteen fifty-eight. A follow-up, Sputnik two in November nineteen fifty-seven, was far heavier at one thousand one hundred kilograms and carried the dog Laika, the first animal in orbit.
